reasoning.text: The render reads instantly as an open-frame FPGA NTT card: ISO shows all eight copper multiplier cylinders, the symmetric dark/brushed add-sub pairs, the blue BRAM stack on the -X edge, the exploded lane and finned heatsink lifted clear, and FRONT/SIDE confirm every part sits on the board with the buses standoff-grounded (no floaters). The single remaining actionable defect from the carried reflection was that the architecture's HEADLINE contribution — radix-4 — existed only in the config-selector spec text, not in geometry: eight radix-2 lanes with prose about fusion, and an exploded 'lane' whose roles even claimed a radix-4 butterfly it did not show. I closed that by enacting the fusion physically (four carbon-fiber radix-4 fusion yokes binding lane-pairs 0-1/2-3/4-5/6-7 into four 4-input BUs) and by rebuilding the exploded cluster into a true radix-4 butterfly (three twiddle multipliers W1/W2/W3, the constant j=psi^512 rotator as a torus, and the y0..y3 add/sub tree), so the X-ray view now teaches the paper's actual datapath. The only residual is inherent to any static scene — the concurrent 9-cycle pipeline cannot be enacted as timed structure — which is a property of the medium, not a fixable scene defect worth >2 points.

fields.before: Elevated broadcast rail running the full depth of the multiplier column, fanning the single fetched twiddle factor down to all eight DSP modular multipliers each cycle so each root of unity is read once and reused; supported on a central standoff post onto the array frame.
fields.after: Elevated broadcast rail running the full depth of the multiplier column, fanning the single fetched twiddle factor down to all eight DSP modular multipliers each cycle so each root of unity is read once and reused; held on the highest of the three routing layers (twiddle 1.72 above return 1.62 above read 1.5) so the read/twiddle/return triad stays legible in plan view, supported on a central standoff post onto the array frame.

fields.before: Operand-read bus carrying source coefficients fetched conflict-free from the crossbar eastward into the DSP multiplier-column inputs; together with the brass twiddle rail and the blue return bus it makes the full read/twiddle/return dataflow triad visible and is the read half of the read-modify-write loop, supported on a standoff post onto the array frame.
fields.after: Operand-read bus carrying source coefficients fetched conflict-free from the crossbar eastward into the DSP multiplier-column inputs; thinned and set on the lowest routing layer (y=1.5) so it reads distinct from the return (1.62) and twiddle (1.72) channels, the read half of the read-modify-write loop, supported on a standoff post onto the array frame.

fields.before: EXPLODED VIEW floating above the array on two riser posts, offset toward the +Z half of the array so it clears the central lanes (3-4) in plan view: one of the eight identical butterfly lanes lifted off the board to expose its left-to-right datapath (DSP multiply -> symmetric add/sub -> pipeline register).
fields.after: EXPLODED VIEW floating above the array on two riser posts, offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes (3-4) in plan view: one of the four fused radix-4 butterfly units lifted off the board to expose its left-to-right datapath (three twiddle multipliers W1/W2/W3 -> constant j-rotator -> y0..y3 add/sub tree -> four-output register).

fields.before: Second support post for the exploded butterfly lane, anchoring the lifted baseplate over the array so it does not read as floating.
fields.after: Second support post for the exploded radix-4 butterfly unit, anchoring the lifted baseplate over the array so it does not read as floating.

fields.before: Exploded view, second stage: symmetric modular adder (dark anodized = the sum path) producing the sum output of the radix-4 butterfly, latched into the pipeline register.
fields.after: Exploded radix-4 BU, sum tree (dark anodized = the sum paths): produces y0 = x0+b'+c'+d' and y2 = x0-b'+c'-d' (mod q) from the multiplier outputs, latched into the register.

fields.before: Exploded view, second stage: symmetric modular subtractor (brushed steel = the difference path) reusing the adder's operands (the ~50% hardware-saving trick), latched into the pipeline register.
fields.after: Exploded radix-4 BU, difference/rotate tree (brushed steel = the difference paths): produces y1 = x0+j*b'-c'-j*d' and y3 = x0-j*b'-c'+j*d' (mod q), reusing the same b'/c'/d' and the j-rotator as the add tree (the ~50% symmetric-operator saving), latched into the register.

fields.before: Exploded view, final stage: pipeline register that latches the butterfly result and feeds the shared modular-reduction spine; this lane is one of eight identical instances on the array below.
fields.after: Exploded radix-4 BU, final stage: pipeline register latching all four outputs y0..y3 before the shared modular-reduction spine; this fused unit is one of four identical radix-4 BUs (eight radix-2 lanes joined by the four fusion yokes) on the array below.

fields.before: Elevated return-routing channel carrying reduced coefficients from the shift/subtract member back across the array to the crossbar, closing the conflict-free read-modify-write loop (reduction -> crossbar -> banks).
fields.after: Elevated return-routing channel carrying reduced coefficients from the shift/subtract member back across the array to the crossbar, closing the conflict-free read-modify-write loop (reduction -> crossbar -> banks); routed along the front edge on the middle layer (y=1.62) so it stays clear of the read and twiddle channels.

fields.before: Configuration register selecting radix (2 or 4) and the number of active parallel butterfly units (up to 8).
fields.after: Configuration register selecting radix (2 or 4) and the number of active parallel butterfly units (up to 8); in radix-4 mode it commands the four fusion yokes to merge lane-pairs into four 4-input radix-4 BUs.

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic; on the -X edge seat the host interface: a PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector feeding a host DMA/PCIe controller block, the boundary where coefficient vectors enter and transformed results leave. 2) Drive the controller into the forward-NTT input FIFO and natural-order output FIFO, then mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks along the left edge at 1.1 m pitch between them. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame); cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (multiply->add/sub->register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view, and clamp the ten-fin exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
